mainTopic: A טמא in the מקדש, speeding up עבודה, entering in an unusual way, and the עשה of נדה with its two חטאות.
overview: The גמרא first asks how a טמא could be liable for staying in the מקדש if he left by the shortest way. אביי answers that on his way out he turned over a limb on the מזבח with a fork, which counts as עבודה, like רב הונא's rule about a זר. Examining רב הונא's rule, the גמרא concludes that anything that speeds up an עבודה is itself an עבודה. Next, רבי אושעיא teaches that someone who enters a בית המנוגע backward stays טהור unless his whole body is inside, because the Torah only counts the normal way of entering. רבא explains that a person fully inside is טמא like the vessels in the house, and a ברייתא about a טמא entering the היכל through the roofs supports the rule. The גמרא then shows that our משנה's words 'זו היא' point back to a משנה in הוריות contrasting the מקדש with נדה. The example for נדה is a man who withdraws immediately, and אמוראים rule he brings two חטאות. רבה begins asking what case this could be, and his search continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How could this case ever happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that the rule is a specific tradition by asking how such a case could ever come about.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say it is learned as a specific tradition, how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the earlier discussion and challenges one position. If the rule is a precise tradition, it seems impossible to find a real case for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view under attack holds that a טמא who stays as long as a bowing is liable even if he does not take longer than the shortest way out. The challenge is practical: if he only goes out by the shortest way, when would he ever add a liable 'staying' to that? The question puts that view in danger of describing a case that can never happen.

keyTerms.meaning: specifically, exactly as stated
it is learned as a received tradition
how can you find it, meaning what real case fits this?

phrases.english: But if you say
that it is learned specifically as a tradition,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier rule that a טמא may stay in the מקדש for as long as it takes to bow.

phrases.english: how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ דַּוְקָא גְּמִירִי, הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about a טמא staying in the מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the rule about staying as long as a bowing is a precise tradition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a person leaves by the shortest way, there seems to be no real case where he could also become liable for staying.

steps.title: אביי: He turned a limb with a fork on the way out
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows a real case: the טמא left by the short way but briefly turned over a limb on the מזבח with a fork, which counts as עבודה, like רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What is the difficulty? You find it where he went out the short way and turned over a limb with a fork. This follows רב הונא, who said: a זר who turns over a limb with a fork is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by describing a real case. The טמא went out the short way but did a quick act of עבודה along the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning a limb over with a fork takes only a moment, so the טמא did not stay longer than the shortest route requires. Still, it counts as real עבודה, so the case exists. אביי supports the point that such a quick act is עבודה with רב הונא's ruling about a זר.

keyTerms.meaning: by the short way out
turned over
a fork used to turn limbs on the מזבח
a non-כהן
liable to death by the hand of Heaven

phrases.english: Abaye said: What is the difficulty?
You can find it, for example,
where he went out by the short way
and turned over a limb with a fork,
and this follows Rav Huna,
as Rav Huna said:
A non-priest who turned over a limb with a fork
is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא? מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ כְּגוֹן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a real case (אוקימתא) that fits the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No case could exist where someone leaving by the short way becomes liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: A quick עבודה done on the way out, like turning a limb with a fork, creates such a case.

steps.title: Restating רב הונא's rule to examine it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רב הונא's ruling so it can analyze it on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב הונא said, a זר who turns over a limb with a fork is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to examine רב הונא's statement by itself. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב הונא was quoted only as support for אביי. Now his rule becomes the main topic. Nothing new is added yet; the גמרא is restating it before analyzing it.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter itself; introduces a closer look at a statement quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Huna said:
A non-priest who turned over a limb with a fork
is liable to death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up רב הונא's ruling, quoted in step 2, to examine it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר who turns over a limb on the מזבח with a fork is חייב מיתה.

steps.title: Either it is obvious or he did nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רב הונא means: if the limb would not burn without turning, the rule is obvious; if it would burn anyway, he did nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If, without his turning, the limbs would not burn, it is obvious. And if, without his turning, they would burn anyway, what has he done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case רב הונא is talking about. It shows that both obvious options seem to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the limb would never burn without turning. Then he clearly did the burning, so why say it? Option two: it would burn anyway. Then his act seems to add nothing, so why is he liable?

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how does it look?
they are consumed by the fire
it is obvious

phrases.english: What is the case?
If, had he not turned it over,
they would not be consumed, it is obvious!
And if, had he not turned them over,
they would also be consumed,
what has he done?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּלָא הַפֵּךְ לַהּ לָא מִיעַכְּלִי – פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling restated in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a זר who turns a limb with a fork is חייב מיתה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: in one case the rule is too obvious to need saying, and in the other his act seems to accomplish nothing.

steps.title: Speeding up an עבודה is itself an עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The case is where turning made the limb burn in one hour instead of two, which teaches that anything that speeds up an עבודה counts as עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a case where, without turning, they would burn in two hours, and now they burn in one hour. This teaches us that anything that brings an עבודה closer is itself an עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a middle case: the limb would burn anyway, but turning it made it burn faster. From this it learns a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea fits neither side of the dilemma. His act did not create the burning, but it sped it up, and that counts as real עבודה. So a זר doing it is liable, and a טמא can do a real עבודה in a moment.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for this case
this is what it teaches us
bringing an עבודה closer, speeding it up
Temple service

steps.whatToRemember: Speeding up an עבודה, like turning a limb so it burns faster, is itself an עבודה. That is why a זר who does it is חייב מיתה, and why אביי's case of the טמא works.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general principle in the laws of עבודה: an act counts as service even if it only speeds up a result that would have happened anyway.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where, if he had not turned them over,
they would be consumed in two hours,
and now they are consumed in one hour;
and this teaches us:
that anything that brings the service closer
is itself service.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא – דְּאִי לָא הַפֵּךְ בְּהוּ מִיעַכְּלִי בְּתַרְתֵּי שָׁעֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: A middle case that avoids both sides of the dilemma.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either turning was the only cause of burning, which makes the rule obvious, or it did nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Turning sped up the burning, and anything that speeds up an עבודה is itself an עבודה.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: Entering a בית המנוגע Backward
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא teaches that someone who enters a בית המנוגע backward stays טהור even if everything but his nose is inside, because the Torah only made the normal way of entering a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: I want to say something, but I'm afraid my colleagues will object. If someone enters a house with צרעת backward, he stays טהור, even if all of him except his nose is inside. The פסוק says 'one who comes into the house,' and that means the Torah only cared about the normal way of coming in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אושעיא. He says that walking into a בית המנוגע backward does not make a person טמא, as long as some part of him stays outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הבא' (one who comes) is read as normal, face-first entering. Walking in backward is not the normal way, so it is not what the Torah meant. The nose staying outside matters, and the next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: A house that has צרעת (a spiritual 'leprosy' affliction) and passes on טומאה
Backward, with his back first
The normal way of entering
I am afraid
Colleagues, fellow scholars

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
I want to say something,
but I am afraid of my colleagues.
One who enters a house afflicted with צרעת
backward,
even if all of him is inside except his nose, he is pure.
As it is written: "And one who comes into the house"
The Torah forbade only the normal way of entering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: בָּעֵינָא דְּאֵימָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the general topic of a טמא entering a holy place or a טמא place, with a new teaching about entering in an unusual way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Entering a בית המנוגע backward, with part of the body still outside, does not make a person טמא, because the Torah means the normal way of entering.

steps.title: The Feared Objection: Then a Whole Body Should Also Be Pure
steps.stepSummary: The objection רבי אושעיא feared: if backward entry doesn't count, then even a person who is completely inside should stay טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I am afraid my colleagues will say: if so, then even if all of him went in, he should also be טהור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the objection רבי אושעיא was afraid of. If walking in backward isn't 'entering,' why does it matter whether his nose is still outside?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason רבי אושעיא gave was about the way of entering, not how much of the body is inside. By that logic, being fully inside backward should also leave him טהור. That would make the 'except his nose' detail meaningless.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
All of him too

phrases.english: And I am afraid of my colleagues, that they will say:
If so, all of him too!
phrases.notes: Meaning: he should stay pure even when his whole body is inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִסְתְּפֵינָא מֵחַבְרַיָּא – אִי הָכִי כּוּלּוֹ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit in רבי אושעיא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The condition 'except his nose' in רבי אושעיא's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only issue is the way of entering, then being fully inside backward should also leave him טהור, so the nose detail should make no difference.

steps.title: רבא: A Whole Person Is No Better Than the Vessels Inside
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a person who is completely inside becomes טמא simply for being in the house, just like vessels that sit inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if all of him is inside, he is no better than the vessels in the house. The פסוק says 'so that everything in the house will not become טמא,' so whatever is fully inside becomes טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רבי אושעיא. A person whose whole body is inside becomes טמא for a different reason: he is simply 'in the house,' like the vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate ways to become טמא here. One is 'entering' (הבא), which needs the normal way. The other is 'being inside,' which works even for vessels that never walked in at all. Once his whole body is inside, the second way applies no matter how he got there.

keyTerms.meaning: Is no worse (his case is not more lenient)
Vessels that are in the house

steps.whatToRemember: Entering backward does not count as 'entering.' But being completely inside makes a person טמא, just like the vessels inside the house.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is saying backward entry counts as entering. He agrees it doesn't. The person becomes טמא only because his whole body is inside.

phrases.english: Rava said:
All of him is no worse than the vessels in the house,
as it is written: "So that all that is in the house shall not become impure."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כּוּלּוֹ – לָא גָּרַע מִכֵּלִים שֶׁבְּבַיִת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a second, separate source of טומאה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If backward entry doesn't count, a person fully inside should also be טהור.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person fully inside is טמא because he is 'in the house' like the vessels. Only someone partly inside who entered backward stays טהור.

steps.title: A ברייתא Supports It: Entering the היכל Through the Roofs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a טמא who enters the היכל through the roofs is exempt, because the Torah only forbade the normal way of entering. This supports רבי אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. On these roofs you may not eat קדשי קדשים or slaughter קדשים קלים. And a טמא who entered the היכל through the roofs is exempt, because the פסוק says 'into the מקדש she shall not come,' and the Torah only forbade the normal way of entering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same idea, 'דרך ביאה אסרה תורה.' It is about the מקדש instead of a house with צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roofs don't have the holiness of the עזרה, so you can't eat or slaughter קדשים there. A טמא who comes into the היכל from the roof didn't enter the normal way, so he is not liable. This shows the same rule as רבי אושעיא's: 'coming in' means the normal way.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
Roofs (of the chambers in the Temple courtyard)
Offerings of the most holy level
Offerings of lesser holiness
The Sanctuary building

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'the Torah forbade only the normal way of entering' is a general rule. It applies both to צרעת and to the מקדש.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
These roofs:
phrases.notes: These are the roofs over the chambers in the Temple courtyard. They don't have the courtyard's holiness.

phrases.english: one may not eat offerings of the most holy level there,
and one may not slaughter offerings of lesser holiness there;

phrases.aramaic: וְטָמֵא שֶׁנִּכְנָס דֶּרֶךְ גַּגִּין לַהֵיכָל – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: and an impure person who entered the Sanctuary by way of the roofs is exempt,
as it is said: "And into the Sanctuary she shall not come"
The Torah forbade only the normal way of entering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי אושעיא's rule from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אושעיא's rule that only the normal way of entering counts
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא exempting a טמא who enters the היכל through the roofs

steps.title: What Does 'This Is' in the משנה Refer To?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, 'This is the מצות עשה in the מקדש for which they are not liable,' and asks what earlier teaching the words 'זו היא' point back to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה says: 'This is the positive מצוה concerning the מקדש for which they are not liable, etc.' Where is the תנא coming from when he says 'This is'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה and starts a new topic. It asks a clarifying question: 'This is' sounds like it points to something said before, so what is it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זו היא' suggests we already heard about a positive מצוה of the מקדש that has no liability. But our משנה never mentioned one before. So the גמרא wants to know where that earlier statement is.

keyTerms.meaning: This is (pointing back to something already mentioned)
A positive commandment
Where is he standing, meaning what is he referring to?

phrases.english: "This is the positive מצוה concerning the Mikdash"
"for which they are not liable, etc."
phrases.notes: 'They' means the סנהדרין. They don't bring a פר offering for a mistaken ruling about this.

phrases.english: What is he referring to
when he says "This is"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of unusual entry and returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier teaching the words 'זו היא' in the משנה point to

steps.title: It Refers to the משנה in הוריות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'זו היא' points to a משנה in הוריות, which says the סנהדרין is not liable for a עשה or לא תעשה of the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is referring to the משנה there: 'They are not liable for a positive מצוה or a prohibition concerning the מקדש...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Our משנה is pointing to a different משנה, in הוריות, which already mentioned a positive מצוה of the מקדש with no liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה in הוריות says the סנהדרין doesn't bring a פר for mistaken rulings about the מצוות of the מקדש. Our משנה now identifies which positive מצוה that was. The quote from הוריות continues in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He is referring to the teaching there (in another place)
A prohibition
Liable (here, to bring an offering)

phrases.english: He is referring to the teaching there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means a משנה in מסכת הוריות.

phrases.english: They are not liable for a positive מצוה
or for a prohibition concerning the Mikdash,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם קָאֵי – אֵין חַיָּיבִין עַל עֲשֵׂה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זו היא' points to the משנה in הוריות, which says the סנהדרין is not liable for the עשה and לא תעשה of the מקדש.

steps.title: The rest of the משנה in הוריות: the מקדש versus נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה in הוריות. For the מקדש, no אשם תלוי is brought. For נדה, there is liability and an אשם תלוי is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not bring a provisional guilt-offering for a positive or negative commandment of the Temple. But they are liable for a positive or negative commandment regarding a נדה, and they bring a provisional guilt-offering for a positive or negative commandment regarding a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the משנה in הוריות from Step 11. It finishes the comparison between the laws of the מקדש and the laws of נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in הוריות sets up two opposite cases. For the מקדש there is no liability for the סנהדרין and no אשם תלוי. For נדה there is liability for the סנהדרין, and an אשם תלוי is brought when someone is unsure whether he sinned. This contrast is the background our משנה's words 'זו היא' refer back to.

keyTerms.meaning: A provisional guilt-offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned
A woman who is טמאה because of menstrual bleeding
A positive commandment (something you must do)
A negative commandment (something you must not do)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement of the גמרא. It is still the quote from the משנה in הוריות that began in Step 11.

phrases.english: And they do not bring a provisional guilt-offering

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: for a positive or negative commandment of the Temple.
But they are liable

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבְּנִדָּה,
phrases.english: for a positive or negative commandment regarding a נדה,
and they bring a provisional guilt-offering

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבְּנִדָּה.
phrases.english: for a positive or negative commandment regarding a נדה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְבִיאִין אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה in הוריות begun in Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The full משנה in הוריות contrasting the מקדש (no liability, no אשם תלוי) with נדה (liability and an אשם תלוי)

steps.title: Our משנה ties back to הוריות and defines the עשה of נדה
steps.stepSummary: Because of the משנה in הוריות, our משנה says 'this is the עשה of the מקדש for which they are not liable.' It then asks which עשה of נדה does bring liability. The answer is a man who withdraws immediately, because withdrawing gives him pleasure like entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on that, our משנה says: This is the positive commandment of the Temple for which they are not liable. And which is the positive commandment regarding a נדה for which they are liable? If a man was having relations with a pure woman and she said to him 'I have become impure,' and he withdrew immediately, he is liable, because his withdrawal gives him pleasure like his entry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that our משנה's words 'זו היא' are answering the משנה in הוריות. It then quotes our משנה's example of the עשה of נדה that does carry liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the question from Step 10. 'זו היא' means 'this is the עשה of the מקדש that הוריות meant.' The matching עשה of נדה is to withdraw only once he is no longer aroused. Withdrawing immediately counts as forbidden relations, because the pleasure of pulling out is like the pleasure of entering.

keyTerms.meaning: Having marital relations
'I have become impure' (she saw menstrual blood)
He withdrew immediately
Pleasure

steps.whatToRemember: 'זו היא' in our משנה points back to הוריות. For the מקדש there is no liability. For נדה there is liability, for example a man who withdraws immediately, since withdrawing is as pleasurable as entering.

phrases.english: And on that, [our משנה] says:
This is the positive commandment of the Temple
for which they are not liable;
and which is the positive commandment regarding a נדה
for which they are liable?
If he was having relations with a pure woman
and she said to him, "I have become impure,"
and he withdrew immediately, he is liable,
phrases.notes: 'Immediately' means while still aroused. The proper way is to stay still and withdraw only after that passes.

phrases.english: because his withdrawal gives him pleasure like his entry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָאָמַר: זוֹ הִיא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the quoted משנה in הוריות back to the wording of our משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה's 'זו היא' answers the משנה in הוריות. The עשה of the מקדש carries no liability, while the עשה of נדה does, as when a man withdraws immediately.

steps.title: Withdrawing immediately makes him liable for two חטאות
steps.stepSummary: אביי, in the name of רבי חייא בר רב, rules that he is liable two. רבא, through a chain from רב הונא, says the same: one for entering and one for withdrawing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: אביי said in the name of רבי חייא בר רב: He is liable for two. And so said רבא, that רב שמואל בר שבא said that רב הונא said: He is liable for two, one for the entry and one for the withdrawal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא ruling about the man from our משנה who withdrew immediately. He is liable to bring two חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה only said 'he is liable.' This ruling adds that he is liable twice. Entering and withdrawing are each counted as a separate act of forbidden relations. Two separate chains of teachers report the same ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable for two (two חטאות)
Entering
Withdrawing

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב:
phrases.english: Abaye said in the name of Rabbi Chiya bar Rav:
He is liable for two.
phrases.notes: He means two חטאות, two sin-offerings.

phrases.english: And so said Rava,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שֶׁבָּא, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: that Rav Shmuel bar Shaba said, that Rav Huna said:
He is liable for two,
one for the entry and one for the withdrawal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אַבָּיֵי אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an אמורא ruling about the number of חטאות in the case from our משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who withdraws immediately after the woman becomes טמאה is liable two חטאות, one for entering and one for withdrawing.

steps.title: רבה asks what case we are talking about
steps.stepSummary: רבה opens a discussion about the ruling that he is liable two. He asks what situation it describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה discussed this: in what case are we talking?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is setting up an investigation. He wants to know in what real-life situation a man could be liable both for entering and for withdrawing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is only brought for a mistake (שוגג). So both the entering and the withdrawing must somehow be mistakes. רבה is about to test possible cases to see which one fits that requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Discussed it, raised questions about it
In what case? About what situation?

steps.confusionAlert: רַבָּה (with a ה) is a different sage from רָבָא (with an א), who was quoted in the previous step.

phrases.english: Rabba discussed this matter:
About what case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case behind the ruling that he is liable two.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what situation could a man be liable a חטאת both for entering and for withdrawing immediately?

steps.title: Suggesting it was near her expected time, and asking who the man is
steps.stepSummary: רבה suggests the case was near her expected time of becoming impure. He then asks what kind of man we are dealing with.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was near her expected time, then with whom are we dealing?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה tries a first possibility: the couple were together close to her expected time (סמוך לוסתה). He immediately asks what kind of man this is, setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Near her expected time, relations are not allowed, because she might become impure at any moment. Whether his actions count as mistakes depends on what he knew. So the answer depends on who the man is.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, if we suggest (introduces a possibility to be tested)
Close to her expected time of becoming impure
A woman's expected, regular time of becoming impure
And with whom? (what kind of person)

phrases.english: If you say it was near her expected time –
phrases.notes: Near this time a couple must stay apart, since she could become impure any moment. They were together anyway.

phrases.english: then with whom are we dealing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible case and narrows the question to the identity of the man.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the man in this near-her-time case: a scholar or someone else?

steps.title: For a תלמיד חכם, withdrawing would be on purpose
steps.stepSummary: If the man is a תלמיד חכם, entering was a mistake, because he thought he could finish in time. Withdrawing immediately, though, would be on purpose, and no קרבן is brought for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is a תלמיד חכם: it makes sense that he is liable for entering, since he thought, "I can finish the relations in time." But why should he be liable for withdrawing? That was on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה tests the possibility that the man is a תלמיד חכם. He shows it doesn't work for the withdrawing part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Entering counts as שוגג (a mistake), because he wrongly thought he would finish before she became impure. Once she became impure, a scholar knows he must not pull out right away. So withdrawing immediately is מזיד, done on purpose. A חטאת is only for mistakes, so he could not be liable two.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar, someone who knows the laws
It makes sense, granted (sets up the part that does NOT make sense)
Entering (the start of relations)
Withdrawing (pulling out)
On purpose, knowingly; no חטאת is brought for this

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the scholar did something allowed. It is that he did it knowingly. A קרבן חטאת only covers mistakes, not on-purpose sins.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule that he is liable two must fit a case where both acts are true mistakes. That pushes רבה to keep looking for the right case.

phrases.english: If you say it is a Torah scholar –
granted, he should be liable for entering,
since he thought, "I can have relations";
phrases.notes: He means he thought he could finish before she became impure, so entering was an honest mistake.

phrases.english: but for withdrawing, why should he be liable?
He did it on purpose!
phrases.notes: A scholar knows he must not pull out right away, so a קרבן, which is only for mistakes, can't apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא בְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם – בִּשְׁלָמָא אַכְּנִיסָה לִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first answer to "with whom?" and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the ruling he is liable two refers to a תלמיד חכם near her expected time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת requires שוגג. A scholar knows he may not withdraw immediately, so his withdrawal is מזיד and cannot bring a second חטאת.
